item.title: Riley Green on Honoring Toby Keith With ‘Think As You Drunk’ & What His Friends Thought: ‘Their Eyes Would Light Up When They’d Hear That Part’
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. We're talking country music and a milestone achievement by Riley Green. He's the first artist since Taylor Swift in 2011 and 2012 to take consecutive solo-written songs to number one on Billboard's Country Airplay chart in 2025.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Riley Green has often been influenced by the likes of Toby Keith, a country music legend known for writing many of his own songs. In fact, Green has covered some of Keith's hits like "Should've Been a Cowboy" and "Courtesy of the Red, White and Blue" in his concerts. Green says Toby Keith's solo writing motivated him to write his own songs, resulting in many solo writes on his records.
[Music transition to a short clip of "As Good as I Once Was" by Toby Keith]
Host: Now, let's talk about Green's latest single, "Think as You Drunk". This song takes inspiration from Toby Keith's style, with a swaggering, midtempo vibe and phrasing that parallels Keith's hit song "As Good as I Once Was". The song even features a posthumous appearance by Keith through a sample of "As Good as I Once Was".
[Music transition to a short clip of "Think as You Drunk" by Riley Green]
Host: According to Green, "Think as You Drunk" was originally cut as an acoustic work tape and evolved into its current form in the studio. The seeds of this song were sown four days before Toby Keith was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame, when Green played a concert in Chicago and writer Erik Dylan started working on the song.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our music update. We'll be back with more news and updates from the world of music.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
